newsitem.title: FRENCH GUIANA: Guiana separatists say France ignoring crime wave.
newsitem.headline: Guiana separatists say France ignoring crime wave.

text.p: Guiana minority separatist leaders accused Paris on Thursday of ignoring a dramatic increase in violent crime that has rocked France's South American territory.

"We are witnessing, once again, a dramatic increase in (violent) crime in our country," Maurice Pindard, president of the Guiana Movement for Decolonisation and Social Emancipation (MDES), told a news conference.
"Every week brings new horrors. Robbery and rape occur daily as well as armed holdups and cold-blooded murder," he said.

"Every time the population mobilises and calls on the (French) state to act, nothing is done. On the contrary, the government systematically uses the population's demands to reinforce police and military presence to crush political opposition," Pindard said.

The capital Cayenne, once a safe and tranquil city of 50,000 on the northeast coast of South America, has become a sea of fear and suspicion. Robbery and rape are commonplace and murder is now a leading cause of death. There is open use and sale of crack and cocaine.
Five French Guianese separatists are in pre-trial detention on suspicion of setting fire to the home of the territory's state prosecutor during riots in November 1996.
The riots left one person dead and caused millions of dollars of property damage, mostly to government buildings.
Their arrests led to a second wave of riots in April and France has flown in hundreds of paramilitary riot police to keep the peace.

French Guiana lags behind mainland France in housing, education and healthcare. Official unemployment exceeds 25 percent and police said Guiana residents are now five times more likely to be victims of crime than in mainland France.
